rulings.ruling: Ruling: representation; project retained. Both apply rules 1 to 6 of Line 3 (i8889 pp. 4-5) with the page 5 Note that a married filer with family coverage at any time figures the additional contribution amount on line 7: the second leaves the $1,000 out of the family amount for any married filer and out of the self-only amount when married with family coverage, the project out of both when married with family coverage. A married filer without family coverage has no family months, so the family amount is not read; the values agree.

(1) The project leaves the $1,000 additional contribution amount off line 3 for a married filer treated as having family coverage at any time, as rule 6 (i8889 p. 4, 'age 55 or older and unmarried or married with self-only HDHP coverage for the entire year') and the page 5 Note ('If you are married and had family coverage at any time during the year, the additional contribution amount is figured on line 7 and is not included on line 3') say; the second puts it on line 3 for every filer. (2) Under the last-month rule with a change of coverage the project applies rule 4, the owner's ruling (amb.2025.hsa_last_month_change). The marital test now reads household.married, the filer's answer, as the instructions' word is 'married', not a filing status.

rulings.ruling: Ruling: representation; project retained. Two differences remain. (1) The second puts the $5,300 self-only amount for age 55 or older on line 3 for every filer; the project leaves out the $1,000 for a married filer treated as having family coverage at any time, as rule 6 ("age 55 or older and unmarried or married with self-only HDHP coverage for the entire year, you can increase the amount ... by $1,000", i8889 p. 4) and the Note (p. 5, "If you are married and had family coverage at any time during the year, the additional contribution amount is figured on line 7 and is not included on line 3") require; the chart's unqualified self-only box (p. 6) is read with that Note, and the second's reading would count the $1,000 again on line 7. (2) The second takes rule 4's greater-of for every filer eligible all twelve months, the project only when the coverage type changed; when it did not change, the December 1 maximum is the chart amount, so the values agree. The second now applies rule 4 to a last-month-rule filer as the project does (amb.2025.hsa_last_month_change, owner ruling), so the earlier split on that reading is gone; married filing separately is refused (f8889.mfs).

rulings.ruling: Ruling: representation; project retained. As ruled before: (1) the project leaves the $1,000 additional contribution amount off line 3 for a married filer treated as having family coverage at any time, as rule 6 (i8889 p. 4, "age 55 or older and unmarried or married with self-only HDHP coverage for the entire year, you can increase the amount ... by $1,000") and the Note (p. 5, "If you are married and had family coverage at any time during the year, the additional contribution amount is figured on line 7 and is not included on line 3") require; (2) rule 4's greater-of agrees in value when the coverage type did not change. The new difference is the last-month rule for a filer eligible all twelve months, the owner's ruling amb.2025.hsa_last_month_all_year (reading 1, i8889 p. 4, rule 2). Medicare months are excluded from the eligible months by the question, as the second's note assumes; married filing separately is refused (f8889.mfs).

rulings.ruling: Ruling: owner ruling (register entry amb.2025.hsa_last_month_all_year, reading 1, accepted 2026-10-22); project retained. The second applies the last-month rule only to a filer not eligible in all twelve months; the project applies it to any filer eligible on December 1 who answers that they use it, as i8889 p. 2, Last-month rule, "You may consider yourself an 'eligible individual' for the entire year if you are an eligible individual on the 1st day of the last month", and p. 4, Line 3, rule 2, "You are treated as having the same HDHP coverage for the entire year as you had on the first day of the last month of your tax year"; the owner chose this reading. The second's note that the spouses' allocations are not checked against each other: they are, by f8889.allocation_bad, which refuses when only one spouse's Form 8889 uses the rule or an agreed allocation, when the two Step 1 limits differ, or when the agreed shares add up to more than the Step 1 limit (i8889 p. 7, Line 6, Step 2, "unless you both agree on a different allocation").

rulings.ruling: Ruling: genuine ambiguity (register entry amb.2025.hsa_last_month_all_year, proposed for the owner); project retained pending the owner. This second transcription applies the last-month rule only to a filer who was not an eligible individual in all twelve months (months eligible under 12); the project applies it to any filer eligible on December 1 who answers that they use it. The text supports both: the rule is open to anyone eligible on December 1 (i8889 p. 2, Last-month rule, "You may consider yourself an 'eligible individual' for the entire year if you are an eligible individual on the 1st day of the last month") and treats such a filer "as having the same HDHP coverage for the entire year as you had on the first day of the last month" (i8889 p. 4, Line 3, rule 2), and p969 p. 6, Example 2 calls the $8,550 of a filer covered all year (self-only, then family from November 1) a contribution made under the last-month rule; but rules 3 and 4 separate a filer who "were" from one who "were considered" eligible for the entire year (i8889 p. 4), and p969 p. 5 limits the same-coverage treatment to months "if you didn't otherwise have coverage". The readings differ only for a filer eligible all year who changed coverage type and answers yes (through Step 1 and the spouse-rule test, as ruled on f8889.step1 and f8889.split). Two further differences, both project retained: the second's Step 4 adds the $1,000 additional contribution amount to each self-only month of a married filer age 55 or older, which the project leaves to line 7 (i8889 p. 5, Note, "If you are married and had family coverage at any time during the year, the additional contribution amount is figured on line 7 and is not included on line 3"), and line 7 counts every eligible month under the owner-accepted reading amb.2025.hsa_line7_months, so adding it in Step 4 as well would count it twice; and with family coverage every month the steps reduce to the first bullet, as ruled before (i8889 p. 7, Line 6).

rulings.ruling: Ruling: genuine ambiguity (register entry amb.2025.hsa_last_month_all_year, proposed for the owner); project retained pending the owner. This second transcription applies the last-month rule only to a filer who was not an eligible individual in all twelve months (months eligible under 12); the project applies it to any filer eligible on December 1 who answers that they use it. The text supports both: the rule is open to anyone eligible on December 1 (i8889 p. 2, Last-month rule, "You may consider yourself an 'eligible individual' for the entire year if you are an eligible individual on the 1st day of the last month") and treats such a filer "as having the same HDHP coverage for the entire year as you had on the first day of the last month" (i8889 p. 4, Line 3, rule 2), and p969 p. 6, Example 2 calls the $8,550 of a filer covered all year (self-only, then family from November 1) a contribution made under the last-month rule; but rules 3 and 4 separate a filer who "were" from one who "were considered" eligible for the entire year (i8889 p. 4), and p969 p. 5 limits the same-coverage treatment to months "if you didn't otherwise have coverage". The readings differ only for a filer eligible all year who changed coverage type and answers yes (through the family-coverage test and the month count). The rest is the recorded reading amb.2025.hsa_line7_months (owner accepted after Stage 13), binding: the second counts only months treated as having family coverage, the project every month treated as eligible (i8889 p. 7, Additional Contribution Amount Worksheet, "$1,000 x number of months eligible", and "If items (1) and (2) apply to all months during 2025, enter $1,000"). Filing status: the second also allows married filing separately, which is refused (f8889.mfs).

rulings.ruling: Ruling: genuine ambiguity (register entry amb.2025.hsa_last_month_all_year, proposed for the owner); project retained pending the owner. This second transcription applies the last-month rule only to a filer who was not an eligible individual in all twelve months (months eligible under 12); the project applies it to any filer eligible on December 1 who answers that they use it. The text supports both: the rule is open to anyone eligible on December 1 (i8889 p. 2, Last-month rule, "You may consider yourself an 'eligible individual' for the entire year if you are an eligible individual on the 1st day of the last month") and treats such a filer "as having the same HDHP coverage for the entire year as you had on the first day of the last month" (i8889 p. 4, Line 3, rule 2), and p969 p. 6, Example 2 calls the $8,550 of a filer covered all year (self-only, then family from November 1) a contribution made under the last-month rule; but rules 3 and 4 separate a filer who "were" from one who "were considered" eligible for the entire year (i8889 p. 4), and p969 p. 5 limits the same-coverage treatment to months "if you didn't otherwise have coverage". The readings differ only for a filer eligible all year who changed coverage type and answers yes (the Step 1 amount this line halves or replaces). Otherwise as ruled before: the second figures Step 3 as Step 1 less the spouse's part, the project takes half of Step 1 or your agreed part directly, equal when the agreed part is at most Step 1, which both require (i8889 p. 7, Line 6, Steps 2 and 3, "Subtract the part of the contribution limit allocated to your spouse in Step 2 from the amount determined in Step 1"); halving rounds half-up to the cent (amb.2025.multiplication_subcent).

rulings.ruling: Ruling: genuine ambiguity (register entry amb.2025.hsa_last_month_all_year, proposed for the owner); project retained pending the owner. This second transcription applies the last-month rule only to a filer who was not an eligible individual in all twelve months (months eligible under 12); the project applies it to any filer eligible on December 1 who answers that they use it. The text supports both: the rule is open to anyone eligible on December 1 (i8889 p. 2, Last-month rule, "You may consider yourself an 'eligible individual' for the entire year if you are an eligible individual on the 1st day of the last month") and treats such a filer "as having the same HDHP coverage for the entire year as you had on the first day of the last month" (i8889 p. 4, Line 3, rule 2), and p969 p. 6, Example 2 calls the $8,550 of a filer covered all year (self-only, then family from November 1) a contribution made under the last-month rule; but rules 3 and 4 separate a filer who "were" from one who "were considered" eligible for the entire year (i8889 p. 4), and p969 p. 5 limits the same-coverage treatment to months "if you didn't otherwise have coverage". The readings differ only for a filer eligible all year who changed coverage type and answers yes; for such a filer with self-only coverage on December 1 the project finds no family coverage at any time and uses line 5, the second applies the spouse rule. Otherwise as ruled before: the second does not test the filing status, the project requires a joint return; married filing separately is refused (f8889.mfs), so within scope the two agree (i8889 p. 7, Line 6, "Spouses who have separate HSAs and had family coverage under an HDHP at any time during 2025").

rulings.ruling: Ruling: genuine ambiguity (register entry amb.2025.hsa_last_month_all_year, proposed for the owner); project retained pending the owner. This second transcription applies the last-month rule only to a filer who was not an eligible individual in all twelve months (months eligible under 12); the project applies it to any filer eligible on December 1 who answers that they use it. The text supports both: the rule is open to anyone eligible on December 1 (i8889 p. 2, Last-month rule, "You may consider yourself an 'eligible individual' for the entire year if you are an eligible individual on the 1st day of the last month") and treats such a filer "as having the same HDHP coverage for the entire year as you had on the first day of the last month" (i8889 p. 4, Line 3, rule 2), and p969 p. 6, Example 2 calls the $8,550 of a filer covered all year (self-only, then family from November 1) a contribution made under the last-month rule; but rules 3 and 4 separate a filer who "were" from one who "were considered" eligible for the entire year (i8889 p. 4), and p969 p. 5 limits the same-coverage treatment to months "if you didn't otherwise have coverage". The readings differ only for a filer eligible all year who changed coverage type and answers yes; then the months "treated as having family coverage" (i8889 p. 7, Line 6, Step 1) are all twelve (December family) or none (December self-only) in the project, the actual family months in the second. The other difference is the one ruled before: the second takes the family monthly amount from its line 3 chart helper, which on a joint return (the only case in which Step 1 is read) is hsa.family, as the project uses.

The second applies the last-month rule only to a filer not eligible in all twelve months; the project applies it to any filer eligible on December 1 who answers that they use it, as i8889 p. 2, Last-month rule, "You may consider yourself an 'eligible individual' for the entire year if you are an eligible individual on the 1st day of the last month", and p. 4, Line 3, rule 2, "You are treated as having the same HDHP coverage for the entire year as you had on the first day of the last month of your tax year"; the owner chose this reading. The other difference is the one ruled before: the second takes the family monthly amount from its line 3 chart helper, which on a joint return (the only case in which Step 1 is read) is hsa.family, as the project uses; married filing separately is refused (f8889.mfs).
